text: But there will still be the busyness of the many different thoughts, a bubbling stream of restless mental activity. This recognition is the second meditation experience of attainment, and it is likened to a river flowing through a narrow canyon. . . . . . The second example of a river flowing through a narrow canyon is used because although a river running through said canyon is still very turbulent and noisy, it is a little slower than a waterfall. If you keep persevering and continue the practice, then you will feel that inwardly the mind's thoughts are slowing down and you are able to remain with the object of focus. However, If you carefully examine, you will see that you are still involved in a continuous stream of many subtle conceptual thoughts or discursive thoughts. At this point, you've reached the third experience called the experience of familiarization, and it is likened to a gently flowing stream. . . When you look at a stream from afar, it seems to be still, and you cannot tell that it is moving. But when you get up close, you'll see that it is moving, alight and rippling. Accordingly then, from this point on, if you don't stop persevering, but keep on striving, you will have less hardship and suffering than before. So exert yourself continuously, we are told. By practicing like this, even the movement of subtle conceptual thoughts will be pacified. And as long as you have the conditioning for the focus, you will be able to remain as long as you like.

title: Shamantha_Meditation_in_the_context_of_TreasuryofBlessing
speaker: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
text: And as long as you have the conditioning for the focus, you will be able to remain as long as you like. Yet this does not mean that you are completely impervious to circumstances. And this then is the fourth meditation experience called the experience of stability, which is like an ocean free from waves, since the mind abides and is stable. . . . . Having reached this far, then without having to undergo great hardships, the fifth meditation experience, perfection, which is likened to a mountain, will arise as long as you continue to familiarize yourself with the state over time. And this then is synonymous with effortless engagement. The mind naturally mixes with whatever you focus on, and without the need for any effort, remains steadily wherever you want it to. Conceptual or discursive thoughts no longer have the power to shake your mind. And this is the accomplishment, is what is called the one-pointedness of a mind of the desire realm. Thank you. And so when we reflect upon the result, which is the one-pointedness or single-pointedness of a mind of the desire realm. So this is the result of a way of training in Khayamavadi meditation, which is levied out according to five experiences of meditation. And so you will recall, I went through earlier the nine mental placements, the result is the same. So these are just different ways of delineation. . . . . . At this time, various experiences resulting from the mind's abiding will also arise.

title: Shamantha_Meditation_in_the_context_of_TreasuryofBlessing
speaker: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
text: So these are just different ways of delineation. . . . . . At this time, various experiences resulting from the mind's abiding will also arise. When you have become familiar with this state, mind and body are said to become supple. As body and mind become workable in this way, whatever objects of focus you settle the mind upon, even if you remain for several days, there is no sense at all of either the body or the mind being unable to cope. The body feels as light as cotton and the mind is pervaded by the bliss of vivid clarity. this subtleness is rough and heavy at first and has a sense of solidity but with familiarity the heaviness fades and there arises an unwavering some shamatha that is extremely fine and clear like a shadow a mind of meditative concentration that is in accord with the main part of the practice. This kind of meditation has the name shamatha, calm abiding, since it is a mind endowed with subtleness. . . . . . this mind also corresponds to the aspect of the first meditative absorptions capable preparatory stage There is nothing that this kind of meditative concentration is incapable of, be it meditation with a conceptual focus or meditation without concepts, as in the meditations on emptiness and the like. There are several ways of counting the stages of accomplishing shamatha. such as the four mental engagements or the six powers. But essentially, they are all included in the following. The mind remains totally concentrated with mindfulness and attentiveness for as long as possible on whichever objects you choose to focus.

title: Shamantha_Meditation_in_the_context_of_TreasuryofBlessing
speaker: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
text: But essentially, they are all included in the following. The mind remains totally concentrated with mindfulness and attentiveness for as long as possible on whichever objects you choose to focus. And as you familiarize yourself with this, the five meditative experiences will arrive. . . . . Accordingly, when you have accomplished shamatha, karma-abiding meditation in this way, the strength of the mind's workability, pliancy if you will, gives the body a gleaming complexion and makes it comfortable and strong. The mind too becomes clear and lucid. and settles on any object of your choice. Body and mind are saturated with immeasurable joy and bliss. The afflictions are reduced and you'll have an experience concordant with the extraordinary joy of inner solitude. By the strength of the merit of practicing this way, with the focus on the form of the Buddha and through the Buddha's blessing, you'll come to see the Buddha, either in actuality or in dreams, receiving the Dharma and all sorts of excellent qualities will arise. And so accordingly, focusing on the form of the Buddha and through the Buddha's blessing, you, the meditator, will ultimately come to see the Buddha either in actuality or in dreams. And thereby, you will receive Dharma teachings and so on. And all sorts of wondrous, excellent qualities of various sorts will arise within you. And so accordingly then, I've given you the teaching, a brief teaching on the method of calm abiding.

title: Shamantha_Meditation_in_the_context_of_TreasuryofBlessing
speaker: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
text: And all sorts of wondrous, excellent qualities of various sorts will arise within you. And so accordingly then, I've given you the teaching, a brief teaching on the method of calm abiding. And so you see, by this, practicing in this way, you'll notice, the text reads, when you have accomplished shamatha in this way, the strength of the mind's workability gives the body a gleaming complexion. And so you can save on makeup. If you look around here at the faces of all of our teachers, you can see in the radiance of their faces, the kind of natural radiance in their faces is reflective of the inner qualities of realization and experience.
